title: Cassandra: partition key, clustering key and writing the query first

videos.script: Cassandra has no query planner that will rescue a bad table. {{ring}} Every row lives where its partition key sends it. The key is hashed to a token, and the token falls on a ring shared by the nodes. You will build that ring: three nodes on your own machine, started one after another. {{nodes}} Then you will ask Cassandra where each customer's orders went, and draw the answer. Inside a partition, the rows are kept sorted by the clustering columns. {{sorted}} So the newest order is the first row, and a month of orders is one slice. Ask for anything the key does not cover, and Cassandra refuses. {{refusals}} Allow filtering makes it run, and a trace shows the price: every node is asked. A storage-attached index makes the query legal, and every node is still asked. {{sai}} So you write the query first, and build one table for each. Last, the partition that never stops growing. {{views}} Ninety days of page views, stored twice. One table keeps them in a single partition on one node. The other splits them by month, across all three. {{sizes}}
